plans.note: Primary review at sec-21; check mutuality of the cap, cap quantum against Fees paid/payable, exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, and whether the 'Excluded Claims' definition in sec-1 carries the standard carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach, wilful misconduct). Cross-check sec-20 so the indemnity is not swallowed by the cap; do not double-flag indemnity scope here.

Vendor indemnity should sit in sec-20; confirm third-party IP infringement plus Vendor negligence/wilful misconduct and data breach cover, defence and control mechanics, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (our data/our unlawful use only). Cross-reference sec-1 'Excluded Claims' and sec-14/sec-15 for IP and data-related indemnity hooks.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant heading in the outline; most likely buried, if anywhere, in Customer Responsibilities (sec-12), the licence/use restrictions (sec-13), scope (sec-2) or General (sec-30). Absence is favourable to us — flag only if a genuine restriction on our business, products or competing purchases appears.

Watch for sole-source or 'all requirements' language in Agreement Structure and Scope (sec-2), Order Forms/Affiliate Orders (sec-4), or bundled with fee commitments in sec-7. Nothing in the outline signals an exclusivity clause; absence favours us.

Direction check only: an MFN in our favour would sit in Fees (sec-7); a burdensome reverse-MFN (obliging us to give Vendor our best terms) would more likely hide in sec-7 or General (sec-30). No indication one exists — do not flag a Customer-favourable MFN.

No standalone heading, so check General (sec-30) and Customer Responsibilities (sec-12), and confidentiality/personnel language in sec-16. If present and binding on us, test duration (12 months or less), limitation to personnel actually engaged on the Services, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Termination rights in sec-9, read with the term structure in sec-8. Confirm we hold convenience termination on reasonable notice with no early-termination fee or penalty (check sec-7 and sec-10 for clawbacks of prepaid Fees or Implementation Fee acceleration), and that Vendor has no mirror right to exit mid-term.

Auto-renewal mechanics in sec-8: test the non-renewal notice window (30–60 days preferred), renewal term length, and any price uplift on renewal (cap/index in sec-7). Notice delivery mechanics in sec-29 are relevant to how we exercise non-renewal; a missing reminder mechanic is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Review sec-28 for governing law (NY, DE, CA or England and Wales acceptable) and forum. Note the Vendor is a UK entity, so England and Wales / English courts would be an accepted outcome; flag only offshore or non-accepted-seat arbitration or an inconvenient foreign venue.

sec-24 is the operative provision: confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger/asset sale without Vendor consent, and that Vendor cannot terminate or reprice on our change of control. Check sec-30 for any conflicting successors/binding-effect language.

Direction check in sec-14 (Deliverables ownership — we should own paid-for Deliverables, with Vendor Technology carved back only as a licence) and sec-15 (we retain title to Customer Data). Watch for any assignment or broad licence of our IP/data to Vendor, including feedback, aggregated-data or model-training rights in sec-13/sec-15; confirm definitions in sec-1.

sec-13 is the grant: test that it extends to our Affiliates and contractors/third-party service providers acting for us, is non-revocable during the term (termination-only, not at-will suspension), and is not narrowed by use restrictions in sec-12 or Affiliate-order mechanics in sec-4.

sec-22 governs audits of us: test frequency (no more than annually), advance written notice (10+ business days), business-hours/off-site-where-possible conduct, confidentiality, and Vendor bearing its own costs absent a material shortfall. sec-23 (Records and Customer Assurance) may extend record-keeping or self-certification duties — read together.

Direction check: service credits running to us (likely in sec-3 service levels) are welcome and should not be flagged. Look for penalties payable by us — late-payment interest or admin penalties in sec-7, early-termination or shortfall charges in sec-9 — and confirm credits are not stated as our sole remedy in a way that conflicts with sec-21.

sec-19 for the performance/conformity warranty: test duration (90 days minimum for Deliverables, continuous for Services), a real remedy (re-performance/repair then refund), and whether disclaimers gut it. Read with acceptance testing in sec-6 and service standards in sec-3.

sec-18 should carry Vendor's coverages; confirm commercial general liability, professional/E&O and cyber cover at market limits, plus certificate and notice-of-cancellation undertakings. Cross-check sec-17 (Information Security) since cyber cover is often tied to the security obligations.

Look for take-or-pay, minimum spend/volume or non-reducible seat counts in Fees (sec-7) and Order Form mechanics (sec-4), and for commitments that ratchet on renewal in sec-8. Acceptable only with a downward-adjustment or exit path; confirm no double-flagging with T4C on early-termination charges.

sec-11 is the transition/data-return provision: confirm a defined assistance period (60–90 days, extendable) at agreed rates, return of Customer Data in a usable format, and certified deletion thereafter. Read with post-termination effects in sec-10 (no data hostage for disputed Fees) and data obligations in sec-15.
